technical_round.label: Technical Depth
technical_round.description: Accuracy, specificity, and density of domain-specific knowledge in answers

technical_round.label: Problem Decomposition
technical_round.description: Ability to break complex problems into structured, solvable sub-problems

high: structured approach (numbered steps or clear phases)
asks clarifying questions before jumping to solution
medium: main cases covered but edge cases missed

technical_round.label: Experience Match
technical_round.description: How well past experience demonstrates the requirements of this specific JD

high: scale matches or exceeds role requirements
specific tools mentioned in JD used in past
low: unable to connect past work to this role

technical_round.label: Gap Awareness
technical_round.description: Honest acknowledgment of skill gaps with constructive framing

high: has a plan to close it

technical_round.label: Scalability Thinking
technical_round.description: Consideration of scale, edge cases, and system behavior under load

founders_round.label: Business Acumen
founders_round.description: Understanding of metrics, business models, growth levers, and unit economics

high: specific business metrics mentioned (CAC, LTV, GMV, NPS)
connects technical decisions to business outcomes

founders_round.label: First Principles Thinking
founders_round.description: Ability to reason from fundamentals rather than pattern-matching to past experience

high: original thought rather than playbook recitation
medium: some original thinking mixed with pattern-matching

founders_round.label: Ambiguity Handling
founders_round.description: Comfort with incomplete information and ability to drive clarity

low: gives up or gives a non-answer

founders_round.label: Ownership Signals
founders_round.description: Language and behavior indicating genuine ownership vs. delegation or deflection

high: uses 'I' for decisions and actions (not just 'we')
identifies problems and drives solutions proactively
low: describes being assigned work rather than taking initiative

founders_round.label: Communication Clarity
founders_round.description: Ability to explain complex ideas simply and compellingly

medium: generally clear but some rambling or jargon

hr_round.label: Cultural Alignment
hr_round.description: Values and working style match to company culture archetype

hr_round.label: Self-Awareness
hr_round.description: Accurate and honest understanding of own strengths and weaknesses

high: honest about real weaknesses (not disguised strengths)

hr_round.label: Conflict Resolution
hr_round.description: Maturity and effectiveness in handling interpersonal and professional conflicts

medium: handled conflict but approach not ideal

hr_round.label: Motivation Authenticity
hr_round.description: Genuine, specific motivations for this role vs. generic or performative answers

high: specific product features or decisions mentioned

hr_round.label: Verbal Fluency
hr_round.description: Confidence, pace, and clarity of spoken expression (voice mode only)

universal.label: STAR Structure
universal.description: Use of Situation-Task-Action-Result framework in behavioral answers

high: Action is clearly the candidate's own

universal.label: Answer Conciseness
universal.description: Answer length appropriateness — neither too brief nor too rambling

universal.label: Consistency
universal.description: Absence of contradictions across answers in the same session

examples: Claims team of 5 in one answer, team of 12 in another
Says worked at company X for 2 years, later says 3 years
Claims solo project in one answer, team project in another

exceptional.label: Exceptional
exceptional.message: Strong candidate — likely to receive an offer

strong.label: Strong
strong.message: Good candidate — likely to proceed to next round

developing.label: Developing
developing.message: Some strengths, clear areas to work on

improvement_suggestions.technical_depth: Practice explaining technical concepts at increasing levels of depth. For each past project, prepare to answer: 'Why this approach?', 'What were the alternatives?', 'What broke and why?', 'What would you do differently?'
improvement_suggestions.star_compliance: Every behavioral answer needs a Result — without it, interviewers don't know if your action worked. Before answering any behavioral question, take 5 seconds to remember the specific outcome. If possible, quantify it.
improvement_suggestions.ownership_signals: Review your answers and count how many times you said 'I' vs 'we'. When describing decisions and actions, use 'I'. Save 'we' for context and collaboration. Practice retelling the same story with explicit ownership language.
improvement_suggestions.answer_conciseness: Record yourself answering questions and time your answers. Aim for 90-150 seconds for behavioral, 60-90 seconds for opinion questions. Practice the 'headline first' technique: state your answer in one sentence, then elaborate.
improvement_suggestions.verbal_fluency: Record yourself and count filler words per minute. Replace fillers with a 1-second pause — silence is more confident than 'um'. Practice answering questions out loud daily, not just in your head.
improvement_suggestions.cultural_alignment: Research the company's engineering blog, product decisions, LinkedIn posts by founders, and recent news. Reference specific decisions or products in your answers — generic enthusiasm is easy to fake; specifics aren't.
improvement_suggestions.motivation_authenticity: Write down 3 specific things this company has done that you admire, and 3 specific ways this role connects to your 5-year vision. Your answer to 'why us' should be specific enough that it wouldn't apply to their competitor.
improvement_suggestions.business_acumen: Practice converting every technical or product decision into a business outcome. Ask: 'What metric does this move?', 'How many users/dollars is this worth?', 'What does the unit economics look like?'
improvement_suggestions.gap_awareness: When you hit a knowledge gap, don't fake it or freeze. Say: 'I haven't worked with X directly, but here's how I'd approach learning it / here's the adjacent experience I have.' Honesty + a plan beats confidence without substance.
